text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing its behavior. The main goal is to make the code easier to read and understand, which helps developers find and fix problems faster. Refactoring also reduces technical debt, which builds up when quick fixes and poor design choices pile up over time. Simple actions like renaming variables, breaking large functions into smaller ones, or removing duplicate code can make a big difference. Although refactoring takes time and effort, it keeps a project healthy and saves the team from bigger problems in the future.
